title: Dyslexia Manifestations
description: Dyslexia manifests across multiple domains including cognitive processing, academic skills, psychological well-being, and neural connectivity. These manifestations vary across individuals and developmental stages.

sections.name: Reading and Language Manifestations
sections.description: The primary manifestations of dyslexia are in word-level reading skills, with specific patterns depending on the type of dyslexia.
keyPoints: Primary difficulties at the word-reading level
Affects phonological awareness, decoding, encoding, and/or oral reading fluency
Distinct from developmental language disorder (DLD), which affects language comprehension

accuracyVsRate.description: Dyslexia can be classified into distinct subtypes based on reading accuracy versus reading rate

characteristics: Selective deficits in phonological and morphological awareness

doublyDisabled.description: Deficits in both accuracy and rate
characteristics: Deficits in both phonological/morphological awareness and RAN
Performance below normal levels on both accuracy and rate measures
Approximately one third of dyslexic subsample

crossLinguistic.description: Manifestations vary across languages and orthographies

manifestations: Less problems with accuracy of word reading
Lack of automaticity in word and non-word reading
Problems in both accuracy and speed of word reading

biliteracy.description: In bilingual children, distinct biliteracy difficulty subtypes exist
biliteracy.dissociative: Difficulties in one language but not the other

sections.name: Cognitive Manifestations
sections.description: Dyslexia is associated with specific cognitive processing deficits that affect reading and related skills.
keyPoints: Reduced structural connectivity between left visual thalamus and left middle temporal area
Deficits in working memory, particularly verbal working memory
Deficits in sustained attention and behavioral inhibition (though less severe than in ADHD)

workingMemory.description: Children with reading disabilities show deficits in working memory
evidence: Particularly pronounced in verbal working memory compared to typically developing peers
May be secondary to phonological processing difficulties

attention.description: Attention deficits are observed but are less severe than in ADHD
evidence: Significant deficits in sustained attention compared to typically developing peers
These deficits are linked to difficulties in word reading and fluency
Less severe than those observed in ADHD + RD group

neuralConnectivity.finding: Reduced structural connectivity between the left visual thalamus (LGN) and left middle temporal area V5/MT
neuralConnectivity.correlation: Strength of this connectivity correlates with rapid naming abilities

sources.title: Altered structural connectivity of the left visual thalamus in developmental dyslexia

sections.name: Psychological and Social Manifestations
sections.description: Dyslexia can have significant psychological and social consequences beyond reading difficulties.
keyPoints: Secondary consequences include reduced reading experience and vocabulary growth
secondaryConsequences: Impeded growth of vocabulary and background knowledge

sources.authors: Catts HW, Haynes CW, Joshi RM
sources.title: Defining dyslexia: 2025 revision

sections.name: Developmental Timing Framework
sections.description: Learning disabilities, including dyslexia, can emerge from maturational asynchrony among interacting systems.
keyPoints: Learning disabilities can emerge from maturational asynchrony among interacting systems
Involves neural, cognitive, linguistic, sensorimotor, and executive systems
Not from isolated deficits within a single domain
implications: Accounts for variable expression across individuals
Suggests interventions should target multiple systems

sources.title: When Development Falls out of Sync: A Developmental Timing Framework for Learning Disabilities

comorbidity.description: Dyslexia frequently co-occurs with other neurodevelopmental disorders

adhd.description: ADHD and dyslexia share a neuroanatomical basis
evidence: Overlapping reductions in cortical area in the orbitofrontal cortex
Unique differences in global white matter integrity in individuals with combined conditions
Shared underlying susceptibility for ADHD and dyslexia

developmentalLanguageDisorder.description: Distinct from dyslexia but frequently co-occurs
evidence: 55% of dyslexic children also met criteria for specific language impairment (SLI)
51% of children with SLI also met criteria for dyslexia

disclaimer: Manifestations vary widely among individuals. These patterns represent research findings at the group level, not deterministic predictions for any individual. Comprehensive assessment is essential for understanding individual profiles.
